{"action":"final","query":{"op":"none","scope":null,"id":null,"text":null,"start":null,"end":null,"offset":null,"derived_op":null,"groupBy":null},"diagnosis":"softmax incorrectly lets keep_dims=False remove the normalization axis from its internal max and sum reductions. Broadcasting aligns the remaining dimensions from the right, so dim=1 on a 2×2 input uses incorrect maxima and denominators. The actual failing output has 4/4 incorrect elements and maximum absolute error 15.605154; the dim=0 control passes with maximum absolute error 3.72529e-9 because trailing-dimension alignment happens to be correct. Retaining the reduced axis in both internal reductions ensures broadcasting along the requested axis and preserves the input shape regardless of keep_dims. The public signature and rounding option remain compatible. Compilation and post-repair device correctness cannot be verified through the supplied API.","locations":[{"source_id":"source-07","start_line":53,"end_line":64},{"source_id":"test-kernel","start_line":4,"end_line":9}],"citations":[{"case_id":"softmax-axis-00","evidence_ids":["observation-softmax-axis-00"]},{"case_id":"softmax-axis-01","evidence_ids":["observation-softmax-axis-01"]}],"edits":[{"source_id":"source-07","old":"    z = x - max(x, _dim, keep_dims=keep_dims)
    num = math.exp(z)
    den = sum(num, _dim, keep_dims=keep_dims)
","new":"    # Keep the normalization axis for broadcasting back to the input shape.
    z = x - max(x, _dim, keep_dims=True)
    num = math.exp(z)
    den = sum(num, _dim, keep_dims=True)
"}]}
